name: Quantisation tables vs camera database
corpus: synthetic photo-like scenes generated from fixed seeds (forensic.validation.run.scene)

detection.task: Do the file's tables match a camera named in EXIF? Is a re-saved file caught?
detection.database: 282 camera models, 370 distinct table sets (built-in plus generated libjpeg)
detection.true_positive_means: files re-saved by libjpeg at quality 70-100 with EXIF still naming one of 282 known models: mismatch flagged
detection.false_positive_means: 331 camera-original files from models with other recorded files, held out one at a time: mismatch wrongly flagged because the database lacks that quality setting

known_failure_modes: The built-in database covers a few hundred camera models, far fewer than commercial databases; labs should add their own reference images.
Cameras have one table set per quality setting; a missing setting causes a false mismatch (see false_positive_rate).
Many devices and programs share tables (libjpeg at a given quality is used by countless apps); a match narrows, never proves, the source.
Anyone can re-save with a camera's tables and edit EXIF.
